about.description: Training analysis of your intervals.icu data on your phone: activities, maps, charts, fitness and form.
about.disclaimer: Veloq is an independent, open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to intervals.icu in any way.
about.mapAttribution: Map tiles provided by OpenStreetMap, swisstopo, IGN, USGS, EOX. Map data copyright OpenStreetMap contributors.
about.title: About & legal

explanations.conditions: Temperature from weather data or your device sensor.
explanations.energy: Estimated energy expenditure from heart rate, power, and duration.
explanations.fitnessImpact: Compared with a rest day, this activity adds load × (1 − e^(−1/{{fitnessDays}})) to fitness and load × (1 − e^(−1/{{fatigueDays}})) to fatigue. Strength training adds fatigue only. Form impact is fitness minus fatigue.
explanations.heartRate: Average heart rate during the activity.
explanations.newGround: The share of the map tiles this activity touched that no earlier activity had touched. Tiles are about 150 to 300 m across, depending on latitude, so this is tile coverage and not distance on new roads.
explanations.activityEftp: The eFTP is intervals.icu's power model estimate for this activity.
explanations.trainingLoad: Training load is computed by intervals.icu from power, heart rate or pace, depending on the data the activity holds and your sport settings. It weighs duration by intensity relative to your threshold.
explanations.yourForm: Your Form (TSB) on this day. This is a daily value based on your overall training, not specific to this activity. TSB = Fitness (CTL) minus Fatigue (ATL).
explanations.speed: Average and maximum speed as intervals.icu stored them for this activity.
explanations.pace: Average and fastest pace as intervals.icu stored them for this activity.
explanations.cadence: Average cadence: crank revolutions per minute on a bike, steps per minute on foot, twice the strides intervals.icu stores, and strokes per minute otherwise.

methodology.prDetection: Compares your latest section time against all previous efforts to detect personal records.
methodology.sectionTrend: Tracks median performance on frequently visited sections over time.
methodology.periodComparison: Compares training metrics so far this week against the same point last week.
methodology.hrvDescription: The 7 calendar days ending today, keeping the days with an HRV reading, and at least five of them. The mean of the older half is compared with the mean of the newer half. A move counts only when its 95% interval, from the spread of your own readings, excludes zero, and it is larger than half a standard deviation of that spread and 2% of the older mean; anything less reads as steady. A steady window still reads as falling when the last two readings are on consecutive days, the second is lower, it sits below the window mean, and the pair passes the same test against the readings before it.
methodology.periodComparisonRestDay: Compares last week against your 4-week average when the current week has no activities yet.
methodology.ftpEstimation: Compares your latest daily eFTP with the value from 30 days earlier. eFTP is intervals.icu's estimate from your power curve, not the FTP setting on your account.
methodology.criticalSpeedDescription: Compares your latest critical speed from the 42-day pace curve with the most recent earlier value that differs from it by more than 0.02 m/s within the previous 90 days, and shows the change as pace.
methodology.efficiencyDescription: Tracks average heart rate multiplied by pace across matched efforts on the section, with an ordinary least squares regression over time. A direction is shown only when the slope's 95% interval excludes zero and the fitted change across the efforts is more than 2% of the mean. A falling value means fewer heartbeats per km: a lower heart rate, a faster pace or both.
methodology.efficiencyFormula: {{quantity}} ({{unit}}) = average heart rate × pace (seconds per km)
methodology.route: Counts attempts on a route in one sport and direction that are timed, not excluded, not partial and inside the route's distance band. A record is the fastest of them, set recently. A trend compares the median of the last three against the three before, from six attempts.

tutorial.firstLoadBody: Veloq reads your activities and wellness from intervals.icu and keeps them on this phone. The first load runs in the background, and your feed fills in as activities arrive.
tutorial.feedBody: Every activity lands here as a card with its map, newest first.
tutorial.feedTip: Pull down to check intervals.icu for new activities, or tap a card to open it.
tutorial.activityBody: Open an activity for its map and charts, its intervals, and the routes and sections it belongs to.
tutorial.notificationsBody: When intervals.icu receives a new activity, Veloq can tell you what it found: a personal best, a time faster than usual, or a step up in fitness. These are examples of what arrives.
tutorial.notificationsOn: Notifications are on. You can change them in Settings.

tutorial.backupLater: You can turn on automatic backup any time in Settings.

sectionHistory.title: History
sectionHistory.boundaries: Why the line ends where it does
sectionHistory.cut_usage_change: Most of the activities that share this ground use it differently from here, turning back, looping or lapping.
sectionHistory.cut_fork: The traffic splits here. Enough of it leaves for another section that the line stops at the junction.
sectionHistory.cut_traffic_cliff: Most of the activities on the busier side never continue past this point.
sectionHistory.cut_trim: The ground past here already belongs to another section, so the line stops where the two would overlap.
sectionHistory.cut_low_support: Fewer of this section's own activities cover the ground past here than the section needs, so the line stops at the last well-covered point.
sectionHistory.cut_terminus: Enough activities start or finish here that the ground beyond is used by different ones, so the line stops where they join or leave.
sectionHistory.cut_pass_end: The pass this line was drawn from ends here. The ground beyond it is counted on its own.
sectionHistory.cut_seam_clip: The line was shortened by {{distance}} where it ran into a busier section. Its counts were taken before the clip.

permissions.locationWhenInUse: Veloq uses your location to record activities, show where you are on the map and sort routes and sections near you. It stays on this phone unless you upload an activity.
permissions.locationBackground: Lets Veloq record an activity you start from Siri, Control Centre or a widget without opening the app first.
permissions.bluetooth: Veloq uses Bluetooth to connect to heart rate, power, and cadence sensors during recording.
permissions.camera: Veloq uses the camera to scan the QR code of a Nextcloud app password.
permissions.microphone: Veloq does not record sound. The camera is used only to scan QR codes.
permissions.faceId: Veloq does not use Face ID.
permissions.motion: Veloq does not read motion data.

permissionNotice.notificationsOff: Notifications are off for Veloq. Turn them on in Settings.
permissionNotice.cameraOff: Camera access is off for Veloq. Turn it on in Settings to scan the code.
permissionNotice.locationOff: Location is off for Veloq. Turn it on in Settings to show where you are.
